proposals.before: Wula Na was notoriously corrupt, squeezed his subordinates for bribes, and winked at foreign pirates, whose vessels clustered outside the Wuhu Gate unchecked.
proposals.after: Wula Na was notoriously corrupt, squeezed his subordinates for bribes, and winked at foreign pirates, whose vessels clustered outside the Five Tiger Gate unchecked.
proposals.reason: Chinese 五虎門 is the Five Tiger Gate near Fuzhou; “Wuhu Gate” wrongly suggests Wuhu (蕪湖).

proposals.before: He sent agents to verify the facts and punished Yisang’a by law.
proposals.after: An imperial commissioner was sent to verify the facts, and Yisang’a was punished by law.
proposals.reason: After Chu’s impeachment, 遣使勘實 is the throne dispatching investigators, not Chu Pengling sending agents.

proposals.before: Vice Minister Zhou Xingdai went to join the inquiry; soon Kui Lun was arrested and granted death, and his son Zhala Fen was banished to Yili.
proposals.after: Vice Minister Zhou Xingdai went to join the inquiry; soon he was arrested to the capital and granted death, and his son Zhala Fen was banished to Yili.
proposals.reason: Source 逮克賜死 is likely 逮京賜死 (arrested to the capital and granted suicide); literal should not invent the name Kui Lun.

decisions.reason: s0008 has 五虎門, the coastal Five Tiger Gate near Fuzhou; Wuhu Gate wrongly evokes 蕪湖 and is a clear mistranslation.
After Chu’s 途次劾 in s0086, s0087’s 遣使勘實，置伊桑阿於法 is the throne sending investigators and punishing by law, not Chu dispatching his own agents.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣使勘實，置伊桑阿於法

decisions.reason: Wikisource and CText match the chapter’s 逮克賜死; 逮京 is unsupported there. Naming Kui Lun correctly resolves the subject from s0026, while the proposal’s “he” could be read as Zhou Xingdai and “arrested to the capital” is awkward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 侍郎周興岱往會鞫，尋逮克賜死，子扎拉芬戍伊犁
